title: The compass at A (the paper’s question)
source: School paper, Q13 (four bar magnets, compass at R and A)
stem:
A compass has a small magnet that can rotate freely. Four bar magnets were arranged such that they were attracted to one another. The compass was then brought near end R and the direction of the compass needle is as shown below.

What would be the direction of the needle when the compass was placed at A?
figure: <svg viewBox="14 10 580 304" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Four bar magnets: two standing side by side on the left, one lying across the top, one standing on the right. End R is the bottom of the leftmost magnet; a compass beside it points down. Position A is beside the bottom of the right-hand magnet."><rect x="150" y="30" width="62" height="200" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="212" y="30" width="62" height="200" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="274" y="30" width="208" height="62" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="420" y="92" width="62" height="200" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><text x="181" y="210" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">R</text><g><circle cx="82" cy="190" r="34" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><g transform="rotate(180 82 190)"><polygon points="82,163.48 73.16,190 90.84,190" style="fill:var(--npole);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polygon points="82,216.52 73.16,190 90.84,190" style="fill:var(--needle-s);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/></g></g><circle cx="548" cy="252" r="36" fill="none" style="stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 6"/><text x="548" y="253" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">A</text><g><circle cx="36" cy="292" r="16" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><g transform="rotate(0 36 292)"><polygon points="36,279.52 31.84,292 40.16,292" style="fill:var(--npole);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polygon points="36,304.48 31.84,292 40.16,292" style="fill:var(--needle-s);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/></g></g><text x="60" y="292" text-anchor="start" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="16" style="fill:var(--muted);font-family:var(--f-label)">Shaded end of needle = north pole</text></svg>
key: Work from the given compass, one joint at a time, then compare A with R: the magnet beside A is the same way round as the magnet beside R, so the needle points the same way.

options.text: N end pointing right, away from the magnet
options.pick: The bottom of the right-hand magnet seems to push the needle’s N end away from it.
options.why: The bottom of the right-hand magnet is S, and a S pole pulls the needle’s N end closer; it never pushes it away. Also, the compass at R shows that a needle beside these magnets lies alongside them, not across them.

options.text: N end pointing up
options.pick: If the top of the right-hand magnet is labelled S (the same as the end of the top magnet it touches), its bottom becomes N, and the needle then lies alongside pointing up.
options.why: The right-hand magnet’s top touches the top magnet right under its S end, and they attract. Unlike poles attract, so that top is N, not S. Its bottom is therefore S, and the needle points down towards it.

options.text: N end pointing down
options.pick: R is S (the needle beside it points down). Magnet 2 is opposite way round to magnet 1, so its top is S. The top magnet: N on the left, S on the right. The right-hand magnet: N at the top, S at the bottom.
options.why: The right-hand magnet is the same way round as magnet 1 (N at the top, S at the bottom), and A sits beside it near its S end, just as the compass sits beside magnet 1 near R. So the needle points the same way as at R: down.

options.text: N end pointing left, at the magnet
options.pick: The bottom of the right-hand magnet is S, and a S pole attracts the needle’s N end, so the needle seems to point straight at it.
options.why: A compass beside a magnet does not point straight at it. Look at the compass at R: it sits beside R, which is also a S pole, and it does not point at R. It lies alongside the magnet, pointing down. A is in the same position beside the same kind of pole.

title: Side by side
stem:
Two bar magnets, P and Q, are placed side by side, touching along their long sides. They stay together. The top end of P is a N pole.

What are the poles of magnet Q?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 240" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Magnets P and Q standing side by side, touching along their long sides. The top of P is N; the top of Q is unknown." style="max-width:330px"><rect x="110" y="20" width="56" height="180" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="166" y="20" width="56" height="180" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><text x="138" y="44" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">N</text><text x="194" y="44" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="18" style="fill:var(--muted);font-family:var(--f-label)">?</text><text x="138" y="220" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="15" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">P</text><text x="194" y="220" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="15" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">Q</text></svg>
key: Two magnets stay together side by side only when they lie opposite ways round, so that N sits beside S.

options.text: Top S, bottom N
options.pick: They stay together, so they attract. Put an unlike pole beside each end of P.
options.why: P’s top (N) is beside Q’s top, so Q’s top must be S. P’s bottom (S) is beside Q’s bottom, so Q’s bottom must be N. Unlike poles attract at both ends.

options.text: Top N, bottom S
options.pick: Lining the magnets up the same way round looks neat, like two magnets end to end.
options.why: Then N sits beside N at the top and S beside S at the bottom. Like poles repel, so the two magnets would push apart, not stay together.

options.text: Top N, bottom N
options.pick: Q’s top is beside P’s N pole, and its bottom is beside P’s S pole, so each end seems to copy something.
options.why: Every magnet has two different poles, one N and one S. A magnet cannot have N at both ends.

options.text: You cannot tell, because the magnets touch along their sides, not at their ends.
options.pick: Chains of magnets are usually drawn end to end, so a side-by-side joint seems to give no clue.
options.why: The poles are still at the ends, and the ends are right beside each other. Magnets that stay together side by side must have unlike poles beside each other.

title: Round the corner
stem:
Magnet X lies across the top. Its right end is a S pole. Magnet Y stands upright with its top end touching the underside of X, right at X’s right end. The two magnets stay together.

What are the poles of magnet Y?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 290" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Magnet X lies across the top; its right end is S. Magnet Y stands upright with its top end touching the underside of X at X's right end." style="max-width:320px"><rect x="40" y="30" width="220" height="56" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="204" y="86" width="56" height="180" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><text x="64" y="58" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="17" style="fill:var(--muted);font-family:var(--f-label)">?</text><text x="236" y="58" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">S</text><text x="150" y="104" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="15" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">X</text><text x="285" y="176" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="15" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">Y</text></svg>
key: At a corner, the end of one magnet sits against the other magnet’s pole. If they stay together, those two poles are unlike.

options.text: Top S, bottom N
options.pick: Y’s top is at the same place as X’s S end, so it seems to take the same label.
options.why: Then S sits against S, and like poles repel: the magnets would push apart. They stay together, so Y’s top must be the unlike pole, N.

options.text: Top N, bottom N
options.pick: Y’s top must be N, and the bottom is far from X, so it seems it could be anything.
options.why: A magnet always has one N and one S pole. If Y’s top is N, its bottom is S.

options.text: You cannot tell, because Y touches the side of X, not its end.
options.pick: Y meets X from below, not end to end, so the rule for touching ends does not seem to apply.
options.why: Y’s top touches X right at X’s right end, where X’s S pole is. They stay together, so they attract, and Y’s top must be N.

options.text: Top N, bottom S
options.pick: They stay together, so the pole touching X’s S end must be N.
options.why: Unlike poles attract. Y’s top is against X’s S pole, so it is N, and Y’s other end, the bottom, is S.

title: A compass beside a magnet
stem:
A bar magnet stands upright with its N pole at the top and its S pole at the bottom. A compass is placed beside the middle of the magnet, on its right.

Which way does the shaded N end of the needle point?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 260" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="An upright bar magnet with N at the top and S at the bottom. A compass sits beside the middle of the magnet, on its right." style="max-width:340px"><rect x="140" y="20" width="60" height="220" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="140" y1="130" x2="200" y2="130" style="stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><text x="170" y="75" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">N</text><text x="170" y="185" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">S</text><circle cx="290" cy="130" r="34" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 6"/><text x="290" y="131" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" style="fill:var(--muted);font-family:var(--f-label)">?</text></svg>
key: Beside a magnet, both poles act on the needle. The N pole pushes the needle’s N end away; the S pole pulls it closer. The needle lies alongside the magnet, N end towards the magnet’s S end.

options.text: Left, straight at the magnet
options.pick: The compass is right beside the magnet, so the needle seems to turn to face it.
options.why: The needle is not pulled towards the magnet as a whole. The N pole above pushes the needle’s N end away from it, downwards, and the S pole below pulls it towards itself, also downwards. So the N end points down.

options.text: Down, alongside the magnet, towards its S end
options.pick: Ask what each pole does to the needle’s N end.
options.why: The N pole at the top repels the needle’s N end, pushing it down. The S pole at the bottom attracts it, pulling it down too. Both agree: the needle lies alongside the magnet, N end pointing down.

options.text: Up, alongside the magnet, towards its N end
options.pick: The needle’s N end seems to go towards the magnet’s N pole, matching N with N.
options.why: Like poles repel. The magnet’s N pole pushes the needle’s N end away from it, so the N end cannot point up towards it.

options.text: Right, away from the magnet
options.pick: The N pole is near, and it pushes the needle’s N end away from the magnet.
options.why: The compass is beside the middle, not past the N end. The N pole above pushes the needle’s N end downwards, away from itself, not sideways. The S pole below pulls it downwards too.

title: Kumar’s compass results
stem:
The ends of a bar magnet are labelled X and Y, but its poles are not marked. Kumar put a compass in three places around it and recorded which way the shaded N end of the needle pointed.

Which is correct?
figure:
Where Kumar put the compassWhich way the shaded N end pointed
On the magnet's line, just past end XAway from the magnet
On the magnet's line, just past end YTowards the magnet
Beside the middle of the magnetAlongside the magnet, towards end Y
key: Off the end of a magnet, the needle points along the magnet’s line: towards a S end, away from a N end. Beside the magnet, it lies alongside, towards the S end. All three results must agree.

options.text: X is a S pole and Y is a N pole.
options.pick: The needle points towards Y in two of the three results, and the N end seems to point at a N pole.
options.why: The needle’s N end is pulled towards a S pole and pushed away from a N pole. It is pushed away from X, so X is N; it is pulled towards Y, so Y is S.

options.text: X is a N pole and Y is a S pole.
options.pick: Use each result in turn, then check they agree.
options.why: Past X the N end is pushed away, so X is N. Past Y the N end is pulled closer, so Y is S. Beside the middle, the needle lies alongside pointing to Y, the S end. All three agree.

options.text: X and Y are both S poles.
options.pick: The needle turns towards the magnet in two places, so both ends seem to attract it.
options.why: A magnet has one N and one S pole. Past X the needle is pushed away, which only a N pole does.

options.text: Kumar made a mistake: beside the middle, the needle should point straight at the magnet.
options.pick: If a compass always points at the nearest part of a magnet, the third result looks wrong.
options.why: Beside the middle, both poles act on the needle: N pushes its N end away, S pulls it closer. So it lies alongside the magnet, towards the S end. The third result is what should happen.

title: Side by side, pushing apart
stem:
Two bar magnets, P and Q, are placed side by side. They push each other apart. The top end of P is a N pole.

What is the top end of Q?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 360 240" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Magnets P and Q standing side by side, pushed slightly apart. The top of P is N; the top of Q is unknown." style="max-width:360px"><rect x="110" y="20" width="56" height="180" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="196" y="20" width="56" height="180" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><text x="138" y="44" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">N</text><text x="224" y="44" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="18" style="fill:var(--muted);font-family:var(--f-label)">?</text><path d="M176 110 h-0" /><text x="181" y="110" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="16" style="fill:var(--muted);font-family:var(--f-label)">← →</text><text x="138" y="220" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="15" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">P</text><text x="224" y="220" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="15" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">Q</text></svg>

options.text: S
options.pick: Side by side, magnets usually lie opposite ways round, so N sits beside S.
options.why: That is how they lie when they attract. These two push apart, so like poles are beside each other: Q’s top is N.

options.text: You cannot tell: magnets side by side do not push or pull each other.
options.pick: The poles are at the ends, and the long sides seem too far from them to matter.
options.why: Two magnets close to each other always push or pull. The question says they push apart.

options.text: N
options.pick: Pushing apart means like poles are beside each other.
options.why: Like poles repel. P’s top is N, so Q’s top, beside it, is N too.

options.text: It has no pole: only the bottom ends are close enough to push.
options.pick: One pair of ends might be doing all the pushing.
options.why: Every magnet has a pole at each end. Q’s top is a pole, and it is beside P’s N pole.

title: Another corner
stem:
Magnet K lies across the top with its N pole on the left and its S pole on the right. Magnet M stands upright with its top end touching the underside of K, right at K’s left end. The two magnets stay together.

What is the bottom end of magnet M?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 290" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="Magnet K lies across the top with its N end on the left and S end on the right. Magnet M stands upright with its top touching the underside of K at K's left end." style="max-width:320px"><rect x="60" y="30" width="220" height="56" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="60" y="86" width="56" height="180" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><text x="84" y="58" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">N</text><text x="256" y="58" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">S</text><text x="170" y="104" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="15" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">K</text><text x="140" y="176" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="15" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">M</text></svg>

options.text: S
options.pick: M’s top is where K’s N end is, so it seems to be N too, which makes the bottom S.
options.why: N against N would repel. They stay together, so M’s top is S and its bottom is N.

options.text: S, because K’s other end is S
options.pick: Both magnets seem to follow the same pattern, N then S.
options.why: Only the poles that meet matter. M’s top meets K’s N pole, so it is S, and M’s bottom is N.

options.text: It has no pole, because it is not touching anything.
options.pick: Only the touching ends seem to need a label.
options.why: Every magnet has a N and a S pole, at its two ends, whether or not they touch anything.

options.text: N
options.pick: Find the pole M’s top is touching, then use unlike poles attract.
options.why: M’s top is against K’s N pole and they attract, so M’s top is S. Its other end, the bottom, is N.

title: Below the middle
stem:
A bar magnet lies flat with its N pole on the left and its S pole on the right. A compass is placed just below the middle of the magnet.

Which way does the shaded N end of the needle point?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 210" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="A bar magnet lying flat, N on the left and S on the right. A compass sits just below the middle of the magnet." style="max-width:320px"><rect x="40" y="40" width="240" height="56" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="160" y1="40" x2="160" y2="96" style="stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><text x="100" y="69" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">N</text><text x="220" y="69" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">S</text><circle cx="160" cy="160" r="34" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 6"/><text x="160" y="161" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" style="fill:var(--muted);font-family:var(--f-label)">?</text></svg>

options.text: Right, alongside the magnet, towards its S end
options.pick: Ask what each pole does to the needle’s N end.
options.why: The N pole on the left pushes the needle’s N end away, to the right. The S pole on the right pulls it closer, also to the right. The needle lies alongside, pointing right.

options.text: Up, straight at the magnet
options.pick: The magnet is just above the compass, so the needle seems to turn to face it.
options.why: Both poles act on the needle, and both turn its N end to the right. It lies alongside the magnet, not across it.

options.text: Left, towards the N end
options.pick: N seems to go with N.
options.why: Like poles repel. The magnet’s N pole pushes the needle’s N end away from it, to the right.

options.text: Down, away from the magnet
options.pick: The magnet seems to push the needle straight away from it.
options.why: The compass is beside the middle. Each pole turns the needle along the magnet, not away from it: N end to the right, towards the S end.

title: On the left of the middle
stem:
A bar magnet stands upright with its S pole at the top and its N pole at the bottom. A compass is placed beside the middle of the magnet, on its left.

Which way does the shaded N end of the needle point?
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 260" width="100%" role="img" aria-label="An upright bar magnet with S at the top and N at the bottom. A compass sits beside the middle of the magnet, on its left." style="max-width:340px"><rect x="160" y="20" width="60" height="220" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="160" y1="130" x2="220" y2="130" style="stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2"/><text x="190" y="75" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">S</text><text x="190" y="185" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" font-weight="700" style="fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--f-label)">N</text><circle cx="50" cy="130" r="34" style="fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--stroke)" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 6"/><text x="50" y="131" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="20" style="fill:var(--muted);font-family:var(--f-label)">?</text></svg>

options.text: Right, straight at the magnet
options.pick: The compass is right beside the magnet, so the needle seems to face it.
options.why: Both poles act on the needle. The S pole above pulls its N end upwards; the N pole below pushes it upwards too. So it points up, alongside the magnet.

options.text: Down, towards the N end
options.pick: N seems to go with N.
options.why: Like poles repel. The magnet’s N pole at the bottom pushes the needle’s N end away from it, upwards.

options.text: Up, alongside the magnet, towards its S end
options.pick: Ask what each pole does to the needle’s N end.
options.why: The S pole at the top attracts the needle’s N end; the N pole at the bottom repels it. Both turn it upwards, so it lies alongside the magnet pointing up, towards the S end.

options.text: Left, away from the magnet
options.pick: The magnet seems to push the needle straight away.
options.why: Beside the middle, the poles turn the needle along the magnet, not away from it. The N end points up, towards the S pole.
